parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Calculate the number of people living in urban areas in Madagascar in 2017.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe two reasons why an increase in the rural population can cause deforestation.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Explain how trees protect the soil from erosion.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
About 300 000 tourists visit Madagascar each year.
Suggest two reasons why the government wants to encourage tourists to visit
Madagascar.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The photograph shows a chameleon found in Madagascar.
There are about 185 different species of chameleon found in the world.
Many tourists visit Madagascar to see the wildlife. Madagascar has 85 endemic species of
chameleon.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the percentage of all species of chameleon that are endemic to Madagascar.
Give your answer to three significant figures.
______ %

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
A survey of Madagascar reported that 66 species of chameleon are threatened with
extinction. Of these species, 22 are critically endangered.
What is the ratio of critically endangered species to species threatened with extinction?

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Each chameleon species is adapted to a particular niche.
Define the term niche.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Chameleons catch and eat insects.
Explain why chameleons are classified as a secondary consumer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An area of mountainous rainforest covering 32 000 hectares has been set up as a wildlife
reserve to protect endemic species, including chameleons. Some tourists visit the wildlife
reserve after a long journey over a rough track. There is a small visitor centre. If tourists stay
overnight they have to sleep in a tent and bring their own food.
The following activities also take place in this reserve:
• plant and animal populations are surveyed by scientists
• trees are replanted by local people
• methods of sustainable farming are taught to local people
• fuel-efficient cooking stoves are promoted.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest how replanting trees can help conserve populations of chameleons.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how sustainable farming in this wildlife reserve can help maintain biodiversity.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
There are about 800 different species of orchid plant found only in Madagascar. Many of
these species are under threat from people collecting plants illegally.
The photograph shows the flower of one species of orchid.
The population of this orchid species was surveyed in the wildlife reserve.
The following method was used:
• one walking track was used as the starting point for the survey
• a global positioning system (GPS) was used to find a starting point on the track
• a transect line was laid out using a 30 m tape due north from the first GPS position
• a 1×1 m quadrat was placed at 5 m intervals along the transect line
• the number of plants of this orchid species was counted in each quadrat
• the method was repeated at two more GPS positions along the track.

2 (a) The photographs show some lychee fruits and some lychee trees.
The fruits grow on trees and are picked by up to 30 000 families in October and November
each year. About 3000 collectors transport the lychees to the main port of Toamasina.
Up to 20 000 tonnes of lychees are exported to Europe each year.
One lychee farmer said,
I like growing and selling lychees at the end of each year. At the end of the year I have
many things to pay for. This means I can support my family.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest three things a lychee farmer could invest in to maintain their farm sustainably.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Everyone in a family is involved in picking lychees. The average family size is 4.7 people
in rural areas.
Estimate the number of people who pick lychees in October and November.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The average family size is 4.5 people in urban areas.
Suggest reasons why the average family size is smaller in urban areas than in rural
areas.
